builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MCF: A Memory- and Communication-Aware Co-Designed Framework for Long-Context LLM Inference
summary: It replaces static KV-cache layouts and prefill-to-decode layout conversion with MARS, which replicates hot KV blocks during early prefill and progressively drains them into a sharded decode-ready layout while routing only lightweight queries across stationary KV shards. Its cost is an FPGA compute-NIC datapath plus a distributed, metadata-driven orchestration layer that is far beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-based stack and adds substantial systems complexity. It can fail when the assumed early-prefill memory headroom or multi-worker communication bottlenecks are absent, and its scaling advantages are unverifiable without a cluster.
rationale: The method targets multi-node clusters with specialized FPGA SmartNIC hardware, so it is relevant to observe but not adoptable or meaningfully testable on the reader's constrained infrastructure.
technique: Stage-adaptive KV-cache layout transitions with in-network routing

claims.statement: It replaces static KV-cache layouts and prefill-to-decode layout conversion with MARS, which replicates hot KV blocks during early prefill and progressively drains them into a sharded decode-ready layout while routing only lightweight queries across stationary KV shards. Its cost is an FPGA compute-NIC datapath plus a distributed, metadata-driven orchestration layer that is far beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-based stack and adds substantial systems complexity. It can fail when the assumed early-prefill memory headroom or multi-worker communication bottlenecks are absent, and its scaling advantages are unverifiable without a cluster.
Improves TTFT, throughput, and scalability over state-of-the-art distributed inference systems, with benefits increasing with context length and cluster size.
